verdicts.quote: "bot" means a conversational chat page inside Salesforce for signed-in org users, opened from the App Launcher. Agentforce agents, Slack, Chatter, Experience Cloud sites, Salesforce mobile and voice are not requested and are out of scope.
the bot reads and writes no business records, so record sharing, object CRUD and FLS requirements are `n/a: no user data records are read or written`.
sharing, object CRUD and field-level security are each stated, not conflated: the bot reads and writes no business records, so record sharing, object CRUD and FLS requirements are `n/a`
a permission set shipped with the product grants everything a user needs: the tab and app, the server operation, and use of the platform credential. A user without it cannot see the entry
verdicts.missing: Who may administer the bot (edit configuration, enter the key) is only 'an administrator'; no permission set or named permission defines admin rights.

verdicts.quote: The conversation lives only in the user's open page. The org stores no message content.
Synchronous callout, no Continuation, no queueable ... the controller makes one synchronous callout with the configured timeout
verdicts.missing: The callout-after-DML and no-callout-from-trigger constraints are not stated, and the design is synchronous, not asynchronous; only 'No DML' (NFR-2) is noted.

verdicts.quote: the key is entered once by an administrator in the org's credential facility. It is never in source files, test code, configuration records, the page, a log line, a debug statement or an error message.
One callout per send (limit 100 per transaction, not approached). Callout wait time is excluded from the 5-second long-running-request limit
verdicts.missing: Heap and CPU time limits are not named or bounded; only callout count and the 120,000 ms timeout are given.

verdicts.quote: Apex tests use an `HttpCalloutMock` (including a throwing variant for timeout and connection failure)
a Named Credential for the xAI host references it. Apex calls `callout:<NamedCredentialName><path>`. ... No Remote Site Setting is needed.
the controller makes one synchronous callout ... and returns when it completes. The page awaits the promise.
verdicts.missing: No asynchronous notification mechanism (platform event, polled status, LMS); the answer is assumed to return inline from the synchronous call.

verdicts.quote: At most one send is in flight per page. A second submit while one is pending (click, Enter, repeated Enter) is ignored and produces no second call.
callout time excluded from the 5-second long-running limit ... Message queues, events and cross-service transactions are not applicable.
xAI HTTP 400, 404, 422 | `INVALID_REQUEST` ... xAI HTTP 5xx | `UPSTREAM` | `Grok is temporarily unavailable. Try again.` | Callout timeout | `TIMEOUT`
xAI HTTP 429 | `RATE_LIMIT` | `Grok is rate limiting requests. Try again in a moment.` ... Retry resends the same text as a new send (one callout). No automatic retry (DD-13).
Maximum wait is the configured timeout (R-9), after which `TIMEOUT` shows. ... the pending state always ends: success, error, or New chat discarding it
verdicts.missing: What happens when a reply is truncated at the 1,024-token cap (a length-limited finish) is not stated.

verdicts.quote: The conversation lives only in the user's open page. The org stores no message content.
verdicts.missing: No stored conversation/turn shape; model identifier and token or usage counts are not recorded anywhere (R-12 logs only code, status, elapsed).

verdicts.quote: no user or bot message text is written to any object, file, platform event or log line by the product. ... Closing or leaving the page discards the conversation.
Request content, in order: the configured system prompt; the bounded history (R-4); the new user message; the configured model id and output-token cap.
At most the last 20 prior messages (DD-4) are sent. The server enforces the bound itself ... If the truncated history would begin with a bot message, that message is dropped too
An empty or whitespace-only message is not sent ... exactly 4,000 characters is accepted; 4,001 is rejected.
the administrator can edit: model id, system prompt, history limit, maximum message length, reply token cap, callout timeout, and the xAI endpoint path.
verdicts.missing: No global switch to turn the bot off (only per-user permission-set unassignment); failed requests are visible only via debug traces.

verdicts.quote: each send emits one log line with: outcome code ..., the xAI HTTP status when there was one, and elapsed milliseconds. ... Out of scope: persistent audit objects
verdicts.missing: No record of who asked what and what was answered, and no audit retention; the spec deliberately excludes it.

verdicts.quote: Out of scope: packaging (managed or unlocked), production deployment, sandbox refresh handling.
verdicts.missing: How configuration and credential differ per environment, and the production code-coverage requirement (AD-12 claims no threshold), are not decided.

verdicts.quote: Wait is bounded by the configured callout timeout (default 60,000 ms, at most 120,000 ms ...). The in-flight indicator is visible before the server call returns (R-11).
States designed, not default: empty (greeting plus a few example prompts ...); loading (the R-11 indicator); error (R-6 messages inline with Retry); disabled and focus states for every control
additive only. Nothing existing in the org is modified or removed.
